facts.value: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26, to Cabinet 22 July 2026 (doc 68016). Fifteen-page annual outturn on Bromsgrove's own book with no appendices (§7, p.15) — one of the smallest treasury reports in the library. The MTFP 2025/26 (February 2025) is the background paper carrying the strategy, capital plan and MRP policy against which this outturn is reported; not on disk. All figures below are machine-checked against the saved text at monitor/papers/mg19/68016.txt.

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 22 July 2026

facts.note: Companion paper on disk for the same council (mg19, doc 67678) is the WRS Joint Board revenue outturn for June 2026, which carries the S151 contact details but no treasury figures. Bromsgrove is being unitarised into a Worcestershire successor authority; §4.4 (p.14) records that the debt and investments transfer to the new unitary on vesting day. No vesting date printed.

facts.value: £31.09m at 31.3.26 (£31.26m at 31.3.25). Forecast to rise to £36.26m at 31.3.27 and £37.71m at 31.3.28. General Fund and Regeneration only — Bromsgrove is non-HRA.

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 22 July 2026

facts.note: Table 1 balance sheet (p.5) for 31.3.25 and 31.3.26 actuals; liability benchmark table (p.11) for 31.3.27 and 31.3.28 forecasts. The CFR movement is small in the outturn year (a £0.17m fall) but the forecast steps up by £5.17m in 2026/27 and another £1.45m in 2027/28 driven by capital expenditure funded by borrowing of £11.10m in the assumption set (§3.46, p.12).

facts.value: £15.00m at 31.3.26 (£0 at 31.3.25). PWLB £10.00m at weighted 4.29% for 1 year; Local authorities short-term £5.00m at weighted 5.3% for 0.25 years. No LOBOs, no bank fixed-term, no long-term LA borrowing.

summary.text:
A small district's clean annual outturn. Bromsgrove's book at 31 March 2026 is one PWLB loan of £10m at 4.29% (matures 5 March 2027) plus £5m of local-authority short-term at 5.3%, £15m total. Our file ties to the pound and the basis point on the PWLB side: loan 909856 MATURITY, £10,000,000 at 4.29%, matures 5 March 2027. The reconciliation opens the email; the £5m LA short-term sits outside our file (we hold PWLB only) and is stated as such rather than glossed.

The interesting shape sits in the liability-benchmark table on page 11. The entire £15m book matures inside 12 months, so 'existing borrowing' runs from £15m at 31.3.26 to £10m at 31.3.27 (after the PWLB matures in March 2027) to £5m at 31.3.28. Meanwhile the benchmark rises with capex from £14.01m to £22.94m to £24.79m across the same three years. So on the paper's own arithmetic, roughly £20m of new external borrowing (or further internal draw on the £14.18m of usable reserves) has to appear by 2027/28. That's the shape the email leads on: not a market-timing critique but the sequencing question about how and when to term any of it out.

Balance-sheet identity holds at both year-ends: 31.09 − 15.00 − 0 = 16.09 at 31.3.26; 31.26 − 0 − 0 = 31.26 at 31.3.25. A minor 72k discrepancy on the Table 1 net-borrowing reconciliation is a rounding artefact across the reserves line; noted in the extract, not raised externally. Rate move since the paper's 31 March reference date is small (11-23 bps higher at the long end, Bank Rate unchanged), so the framing is refinancing shape, not market-move.

Local Government Reorganisation is context, not a hook: §4.4 records that Bromsgrove's debt and investments transfer to the new Worcestershire unitary on vesting day. The £10m PWLB matures March 2027 and the £5m LA short-term rolls quarterly, so most of the current book will naturally have moved off before any plausible vesting date. Refinancing decisions between now and then still sit at Bromsgrove.

Officer address on this paper is Debra Goodall (Assistant Director of Finance and Customer Services, Deputy S151) at Debra.Goodall@bromsgroveandredditch.gov.uk (page 1 header table — the page 15 author block prints a slightly different domain with a 'bc' suffix, treated as a transcription glitch; the page 1 form matches James Walton's on the earlier mg19 paper, doc 67678). James Walton is the substantive S151 for both Bromsgrove and Redditch per that earlier paper — the current paper is unambiguously about Bromsgrove so an email about it is unambiguous, but he sits on the from-line only if a copy is warranted. Email drafted to Debra directly since she authored the paper; James copied.

officer.subject: Your one PWLB loan matches our file — and £20m opens under your own benchmark by 2028
officer.body:
Hi Debra,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the outturn that went to Cabinet on 22 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. It's a compact and unusually clean paper for its length, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

The first thing worth saying is a reconciliation. Your Table 3 on page 7 shows one PWLB loan of £10.00m at a 4.29% weighted rate with one year weighted average maturity. Our file agrees to the pound and the basis point: one loan of £10,000,000 at 4.29%, maturity profile, maturing 5 March 2027 — about seven months from today. Your £5m of local-authority short-term borrowing sits outside our file since we hold PWLB only, but the PWLB side ties exactly.

The shape that follows from that is where the interesting question sits. Your maturity table on page 12 has 100% of the £15m book under twelve months, and your liability benchmark on page 11 forecasts loans CFR rising from £31.09m at year-end to £36.26m by 31.3.27 and £37.71m by 31.3.28, while existing borrowing runs off from £15m to £10m to £5m across the same three year-ends. That leaves a benchmark of £24.79m against £5m of existing borrowing at 31 March 2028 — roughly £20m to find over 2027/28 from some combination of new external borrowing and further internal draw on the £14.18m of usable reserves. Not a market-timing point so much as a sequencing one: how you weight short-dated local-authority lending against terming any of it out via PWLB will move your carry more over the next eighteen months than the level of the fifty-year curve does. Your own paragraph 3.28 captures the range on the LA-to-LA side neatly — 4.0-4.5% for most of the year, then 5.0-7.0% at year-end — and that spread against the PWLB curve is the live trade-off.

On where the market has moved since your paper's 31 March reference date, it hasn't materially. Five-year PWLB certainty is up about 6 basis points today, ten-year up 11, and fifty-year up 23, with Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% — the Arlingclose view your paragraph 3.12 records has, so far, been what the MPC has actually done. So the rate landscape framing your outturn's page 14 table is still, more or less, the one facing any decision today.

The pages that go with all this: today's rates at both fixings and the whole curve are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard; the monthly sector breakdown at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity shows what everyone else is drawing (July 2026 was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers, average 5.02%); and pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis prices your PWLB position daily against the DMO's repayment curve. Our liability-benchmark pathway — five courses, interactive, built on live data — is directly relevant to what your page 11 forecasts, and to CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates.

Free accounts for the whole team, and our 115 courses — officers and members, SONIA through to the Prudential Code — are free to local authorities until the end of September. Three that fit your position: PWLB rates and the certainty discount, Cost of carry and internal borrowing (for the £16.09m your Table 1 carries at year-end), and Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) for members who scrutinise treasury papers.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
